newsitem.title: CHILE: Soquimich to raise sodium sulfate output.
newsitem.headline: Soquimich to raise sodium sulfate output.

text.p: Chilean nitrate maker Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile SA, or Soquimich, will invest $6 million to raise its sodium sulfate output to 110,000 tonnes next year from an expected 70,000 tonnes this year, it said.
Soquimich makes sodium sulfate as a byproduct of natural nitrates and iodine and is among the world's cheapest-cost producers of the substance, Soquimich said in a statement.
The average price for the additional tonnes will be between $80 and $90 per tonne FOB in bulk at Tocopilla port, it said.
Soquimich last year produced about 40,000 tonnes of sodium sulfate, it added.
